240: I check books out, I check books in. The excitement rarely peaks in between.
241: All day I move books six inches to the left, then back again.
242: My job is a book comes, a book goes. I am the small door it passes through.
243: I set the date stamp each morning. It is the single most powerful decision of my day.
244: The most dramatic thing here is a book returned one day late.
245: I've handled ten thousand books today and read the spine of none of them.
246: Books come to me full of stories. I only ever check the little card.
247: It is very quiet work. My biggest decision is which stamp needs more ink.
248: Books drop through the return slot all night. I like to imagine they had adventures.
249: A visitor owed a fine of two coins today. We discussed it as though it were a fortune.
250: A book goes out. A week later it returns. This is my entire tide.
251: I know where every book lives. I've simply never opened one to find out why.
252: The days are calm. A cart with a squeaky wheel is a genuine event.
253: The hold shelf is where books wait for people who requested them and then vanished forever.
254: Someone renewed the same book all year. Neither of us truly believes they will read it.
255: I've perfected the quiet slide of a book across a desk. It took years.
256: I stack the return cart very neatly. Nobody has ever noticed. I keep doing it anyway.
257: I own a stamp, a pencil, and a very small bell. A wild day is when I get to use all three.
258: I issued a new library card today. Briefly, I felt like I was handing over a great privilege.
259: By closing I have spoken perhaps nine words, four of them concerning a stapler.
260: I spend half my day whispering 'quiet' and the other half knowing everything.
261: People approach my desk of near-infinite knowledge to ask where the printer is.
262: The reading room is meant for deep research. Mostly it hosts very dignified naps.
263: I give people the precisely correct answer. Half of them decide to disagree with it anyway.
264: A visitor once asked a question I actually had to look up. It was the finest moment of my year.
265: I once answered a question so obscure I surprised myself. Then I shushed a cough.
266: I sit at a desk built for the hardest questions. Today's hardest was what the date is.
267: I dust encyclopedias last opened before I was born. Over the years, we have grown close.
268: Someone asked one small question. I delivered the entire history. They slowly backed away.
269: People are amazed I know so much. I'm amazed anyone here can hear me at all.
270: I answer questions all day at a volume slightly below a passing cloud.
271: I can find any book from memory. The catalog and I compete politely, and I am winning.
272: Some days a single person visits my desk. I treat their question as a royal audience.
273: I hold a great many facts, and I frown, very quietly, at loud shoes.
274: I once corrected a footnote that no one will ever read. It remains my proudest achievement.
275: I could win any argument. I would simply do it too quietly for anyone to notice.
276: People forget I'm here until they need a fact. Then I appear, softly, with three.
277: I hush the room, then answer a stranger's question about the entire universe.
278: The louder the question, the quieter I answer. It's a small act of protest.
279: People whisper their questions to me as if the books nearby might overhear and grow jealous.
